claim: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is a rare human genetic disorder characterized by altered skeletal development and extraskeletal ossification.
source: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is a rare human genetic disorder characterized by altered skeletal development and extraskeletal ossification.
evidence: This is a well-established characterization of FOP cited in the introduction with references to prior literature.

claim: All cases of FOP are caused by activating mutations in the type I BMP/TGFβ cell surface receptor ACVR1.
source: All cases of FOP are caused by activating mutations in the type I BMP/TGFβ cell surface receptor ACVR1, which over-activates signaling through phospho-Smad1/5 (pSmad1/5).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research establishing the genetic basis of FOP.

claim: FOP-causing ACVR1 mutations over-activate signaling through phospho-Smad1/5 (pSmad1/5).
source: All cases of FOP are caused by activating mutations in the type I BMP/TGFβ cell surface receptor ACVR1, which over-activates signaling through phospho-Smad1/5 (pSmad1/5).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies demonstrating the signaling mechanism.

claim: The FOP mutants ACVR1-R206H and -G328R do not require their ligand binding domain to over-activate BMP signaling in DV patterning.
source: We determined that the FOP mutants ACVR1-R206H and -G328R do not require their ligand binding domain to over-activate BMP signaling in DV patterning.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Intact ACVR1-R206H has the ability to respond to both Bmp7 and Activin A ligands.
source: However, intact ACVR1-R206H has the ability to respond to both Bmp7 and Activin A ligands.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: BMPR1, a type I BMP receptor normally required for BMP-mediated patterning of the embryo, is dispensable for both ligand-independent signaling pathway activation and ligand-responsive signaling hyperactivation by ACVR1-R206H.
source: Additionally, BMPR1, a type I BMP receptor normally required for BMP-mediated patterning of the embryo, is dispensable for both ligand-independent signaling pathway activation and ligand-responsive signaling hyperactivation by ACVR1-R206H.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figures 5, 6, and 7.

claim: FOP-ACVR1 is not constrained by the same receptor/ligand partner requirements as WT-ACVR1.
source: These results demonstrate that FOP-ACVR1 is not constrained by the same receptor/ligand partner requirements as WT-ACVR1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings presented in the study.

claim: Most cases of FOP are caused by a single amino acid substitution, R206H, in ACVR1.
source: Most cases of FOP are caused by a single amino acid substitution, R206H, in the type I BMP/TGFβ cell surface receptor ACVR1 (also known as ALK2), which over-activates signaling through phospho-Smad1/5 (pSmad1/5) (Shore et al., 2006; Shen et al., 2009; van Dinther et al., 2010; Fukuda et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: A small subset of patients with variant presentation of the classical FOP phenotype have distinct activating mutations in the ACVR1 gene, including the substitution G328R.
source: A small subset of patients with variant presentation of the classical FOP phenotype have distinct activating mutations in the ACVR1 gene, including the substitution G328R (Kaplan et al., 2009; Haupt et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The phenotypic consequences of increased ACVR1 signaling have been well characterized in both patients and animal models.
source: While the phenotypic consequences of increased ACVR1 signaling have been well characterized in both patients and animal models (Casal et al., 2019; Pignolo et al., 2011; Chakkalakal and Shore, 2019), the mechanism by which ACVR1 mutations lead to over-active signaling is less well understood.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The mechanism by which ACVR1 mutations lead to over-active signaling is less well understood.
source: While the phenotypic consequences of increased ACVR1 signaling have been well characterized in both patients and animal models (Casal et al., 2019; Pignolo et al., 2011; Chakkalakal and Shore, 2019), the mechanism by which ACVR1 mutations lead to over-active signaling is less well understood.
evidence: This statement establishes the knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: ACVR1 and its signaling partners belong to the transforming growth factor beta (TGFβ) superfamily.
source: ACVR1 and its signaling partners belong to the transforming growth factor beta (TGFβ) superfamily.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: The activity of ACVR1 is critical to several developmental processes including embryonic patterning and skeletal formation.
source: The activity of ACVR1 is critical to several developmental processes including embryonic patterning and skeletal formation (Derynck and Akhurst, 2007; Little and Mullins, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In zebrafish, Acvr1l forms a tetrameric receptor complex with one other type I BMP receptor, Bmpr1a or Bmpr1b, and two type II BMP receptors.
source: In zebrafish, Acvr1l (also known as Alk8), the zebrafish paralog to human and mouse ACVR1 (Yelick et al., 1998), forms a tetrameric receptor complex with one other type I BMP receptor, Bmpr1a or Bmpr1b (also known as Alk3 and Alk6, respectively), and two type II BMP receptors (Little and Mullins, 2006; Ehrlich et al., 2011; Yadin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Receptor complex assembly allows the type II BMP receptors to phosphorylate the type I receptors at serine/threonine residues within the GS domain.
source: Receptor complex assembly allows the type II BMP receptors to phosphorylate the type I receptors at serine/threonine residues within the GS domain (Schmierer and Hill, 2007; Shi and Massagué, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Phosphorylation of the type I BMP receptors results in a conformational change, allowing them to bind ATP and phosphorylate Smad1/5 to initiate downstream transcription.
source: Phosphorylation of the type I BMP receptors results in a conformational change, allowing them to bind ATP and phosphorylate Smad1/5 to initiate downstream transcription (Feng and Derynck, 2005; Chaikuad et al., 2012; Liu et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The zebrafish embryo is an excellent genetically tractable in vivo vertebrate model for investigating the signaling mechanism of the ACVR1-FOP receptor.
source: The zebrafish embryo is an excellent genetically tractable in vivo vertebrate model for investigating the signaling mechanism of the ACVR1-FOP receptor (Shen et al., 2009; Mucha et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In the early zebrafish embryo, BMP acts as a morphogen to pattern the dorsoventral (DV) axis in a process that is conserved throughout the animal kingdom.
source: In the early zebrafish embryo, BMP acts as a morphogen to pattern the dorsoventral (DV) axis in a process that is conserved throughout the animal kingdom (Zinski et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: High levels of BMP signaling specify ventral cell fates and intermediate signaling specifies lateral fates, while absence of signaling allows dorsal cell fate specification.
source: High levels of BMP signaling specify ventral cell fates and intermediate signaling specifies lateral fates, while absence of signaling allows dorsal cell fate specification.
evidence: This is established knowledge about zebrafish DV patterning.

claim: The DV pattern is generated through a quantifiable pSmad1/5 signaling gradient within the gastrulating embryo that peaks ventrally and decreases dorsally.
source: The DV pattern is generated through a quantifiable pSmad1/5 signaling gradient within the gastrulating embryo that peaks ventrally and decreases dorsally (Little and Mullins, 2006; Zinski et al., 2017; Zinski et al., 2019; Tucker et al., 2008; Mintzer et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Perturbations to the BMP signaling gradient in the developing embryo result in distinct, dose-dependent patterning phenotypes.
source: Perturbations to this BMP signaling gradient in the developing embryo result in distinct, dose-dependent patterning phenotypes (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is supported by reference to Figure 1b showing the phenotypes.

claim: Over-activation of the BMP signaling pathway by FOP-ACVR1 causes ventralization, an excess of ventral cell fate specification at the expense of dorsal fates.
source: Over-activation of the BMP signaling pathway by FOP-ACVR1 causes ventralization, an excess of ventral cell fate specification at the expense of dorsal fates (Shen et al., 2009; Mucha et al., 2018), while loss of endogenous acvr1l expression leads to an opposite dorsalization.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Loss of endogenous acvr1l expression leads to dorsalization.
source: Over-activation of the BMP signaling pathway by FOP-ACVR1 causes ventralization, an excess of ventral cell fate specification at the expense of dorsal fates (Shen et al., 2009; Mucha et al., 2018), while loss of endogenous acvr1l expression leads to an opposite dorsalization.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Loss of acvr1l in the zebrafish can be rescued by human ACVR1, demonstrating their conserved activity.
source: Loss of acvr1l in the zebrafish can be rescued by human ACVR1, demonstrating their conserved activity (Shen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Previous work demonstrated that expression of ACVR1-R206H in the zebrafish embryo over-activates BMP signaling in the absence of Bmp2 and Bmp7, the obligatory patterning ligands of the developing zebrafish.
source: Previous work by our lab demonstrated that expression of ACVR1-R206H in the zebrafish embryo over-activates BMP signaling in the absence of Bmp2 and Bmp7, the obligatory patterning ligands of the developing zebrafish (Shen et al., 2009; Little and Mullins, 2009; Nguyen et al., 1998; Dick et al., 2000; Schmid et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: ACVR1-R206H shows acquired responsiveness to Activin A, a TGFβ superfamily ligand that normally signals through ACVR1b and pSmad2/3.
source: Surprisingly, ACVR1-R206H shows acquired responsiveness to novel ligands in cell culture and mouse models; most notably Activin A, a TGFβ superfamily ligand that normally signals through ACVR1b (also called ALK4) and pSmad2/3 (Hatsell et al., 2015; Lees-Shepard et al., 2018; Hino et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: ACVR1-R206H has been shown to require its normal type II BMP receptor partners, BMPR2 and ACVR2a.
source: While ACVR1-R206H has been shown to require its normal type II BMP receptor partners, BMPR2 and ACVR2a (Hino et al., 2015; Bagarova et al., 2013), it is unknown whether it retains a requirement for its type I BMP receptor partner, BMPR1.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: It is unknown whether ACVR1-R206H retains a requirement for its type I BMP receptor partner, BMPR1.
source: While ACVR1-R206H has been shown to require its normal type II BMP receptor partners, BMPR2 and ACVR2a (Hino et al., 2015; Bagarova et al., 2013), it is unknown whether it retains a requirement for its type I BMP receptor partner, BMPR1.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: ACVR1-R206H has been shown to signal in the absence of BMPR1a or BMPR1b individually.
source: ACVR1-R206H has been shown to signal in the absence of BMPR1a or BMPR1b individually (Hino et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The ability of FOP-ACVR1 to function in the absence of both BMPR1a and BMPR1b has not been tested.
source: However, the ability of FOP-ACVR1 to function in the absence of both BMPR1a and BMPR1b, which largely function redundantly (Yoon et al., 2005; Wine-Lee et al., 2004), has not been tested.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: BMPR1a and BMPR1b largely function redundantly.
source: However, the ability of FOP-ACVR1 to function in the absence of both BMPR1a and BMPR1b, which largely function redundantly (Yoon et al., 2005; Wine-Lee et al., 2004), has not been tested.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Ligand-binding domain-deficient ACVR1-R206H and -G328R can over-activate pSmad1/5 signaling.
source: We show that ligand-binding domain-deficient ACVR1-R206H and -G328R can over-activate pSmad1/5 signaling, demonstrating that these mutant receptors have enhanced signaling activity in the absence of ligand binding.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: ACVR1-R206H and -G328R mutant receptors have enhanced signaling activity in the absence of ligand binding.
source: We show that ligand-binding domain-deficient ACVR1-R206H and -G328R can over-activate pSmad1/5 signaling, demonstrating that these mutant receptors have enhanced signaling activity in the absence of ligand binding.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Intact ACVR1-R206H shows hyperactive pSmad1/5 signaling in response to Bmp7 and Activin A ligands.
source: However, intact ACVR1-R206H shows hyperactive pSmad1/5 signaling in response to Bmp7 and Activin A ligands.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Neither the ligand-independent nor the ligand-responsive signaling modalities of ACVR1-R206H require the partner type I BMP receptors that are necessary for signaling by wild-type ACVR1.
source: We further determined that neither the ligand-independent nor the ligand-responsive signaling modalities of ACVR1-R206H require the partner type I BMP receptors that are necessary for signaling by wild-type ACVR1.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The ACVR1-R206H and G328R receptors have acquired a fundamentally altered signaling mechanism.
source: These results demonstrate that the ACVR1-R206H and ﻿G328R receptors have acquired a fundamentally altered signaling mechanism.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: All ACVR1 protein variants, regardless of their signaling activity, were expressed and localized to the cell membrane within the developing embryo.
source: We found that all the ACVR1 protein variants, regardless of their signaling activity, were expressed and localized to the cell membrane within the developing embryo (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Knockdown of Acvr1l generates the severely dorsalized C5 phenotype, consistent with the loss of all BMP pathway activity.
source: As previously demonstrated and re-confirmed here, knockdown of Acvr1l generates the identical, severely dorsalized C5 phenotype as the maternal-zygotic acvr1l null mutant, consistent with the loss of all BMP pathway activity (Figure 1d and column four in Figure 1e–f; Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Mintzer et al., 2001; Little and Mullins, 2009; Bauer et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in figures and citations to prior research.

claim: Injection of wild-type mouse Acvr1 mRNA can fully rescue the C5 dorsalized phenotype caused by Acvr1l knockdown.
source: Importantly, injection of wild-type mouse Acvr1 mRNA can fully rescue this phenotype (Figure 1e,e', compare to d), demonstrating the specificity of the knockdown for Acvr1l.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Wild-type ACVR1 rescued loss of endogenous Acvr1l, primarily to wild-type or mildly dorsalized phenotypes.
source: While ACVR1 rescued loss of endogenous Acvr1l, primarily to wild-type or mildly dorsalized phenotypes (Figure 1e column 5, Figure 1e'; Figure 1—figure supplement 1), ΔAcvr1 did not (Figure 1e column 6, and Figure 1e'; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: ΔAcvr1 did not rescue loss of endogenous Acvr1l.
source: While ACVR1 rescued loss of endogenous Acvr1l, primarily to wild-type or mildly dorsalized phenotypes (Figure 1e column 5, Figure 1e'; Figure 1—figure supplement 1), ΔAcvr1 did not (Figure 1e column 6, and Figure 1e'; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Both Acvr1-R206H and ΔAcvr1-R206H ventralized WT and acvr1l-KD zebrafish embryos.
source: By contrast, both Acvr1-R206H and ΔAcvr1-R206H ventralized WT and acvr1l-KD zebrafish embryos (Figure 1f columns 2, 3, 5 and 6, Figure 1f'; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Both Acvr1-G328R and ΔAcvr1-G328R ventralized WT and acvr1l-KD embryos.
source: Likewise, both Acvr1-G328R and ΔAcvr1-G328R ventralized WT and acvr1l-KD embryos (Figure 1g columns 2, 3, 5 and 6, Figure 1g'; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The results in an in vivo vertebrate model support that ACVR1-R206H and ACVR1-G328R exhibit ligand-independent signaling activity.
source: These results in an in vivo vertebrate model support that ACVR1-R206H and ACVR1-G328R, unlike wild type ACVR1, exhibit ligand-independent signaling activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: The amount of Acvr1-R206H or -G328R required to ventralize the zebrafish embryo is similar to or lower than the amount of Acvr1 required to pattern the wild-type zebrafish, regardless of the presence of a ligand-binding domain.
source: These results show that the amount of Acvr1-R206H or -G328R required to ventralize the zebrafish embryo is similar to or lower than the amount of Acvr1 required to pattern the wild-type zebrafish, regardless of the presence of a ligand-binding domain.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ventralization by FOP mutant receptors is not due to overexpression of the FOP mutant receptors.
source: Altogether, the results indicate that the ventralization is not due to overexpression of the FOP mutant receptors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the receptor expression level analysis.

claim: A nuclear gradient of pSmad1/5 activity forms across the DV axis of the zebrafish embryo in response to BMP signaling during early embryonic development.
source: During early embryonic development, a nuclear gradient of pSmad1/5 activity forms across the DV axis of the zebrafish embryo in response to BMP signaling (Zinski et al., 2017; Zinski et al., 2019; Tucker et al., 2008; Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research and Figure 2a.

claim: The pSmad1/5 gradient persists throughout gastrulation and specifies DV axial fates.
source: This gradient persists throughout gastrulation and specifies DV axial fates.
evidence: This is established knowledge about zebrafish development.

claim: Wild-type embryos formed a gradient of pSmad1/5 expression that peaks ventrally and decreases dorsally.
source: While wild-type embryos formed a gradient of pSmad1/5 expression that peaks ventrally and decreases dorsally (Figure 2a; Mucha et al., 2018), Acvr1l-KD embryos lacked detectable pSmad1/5 signal (Figure 2a').
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a and a citation.

claim: Acvr1l-KD embryos lacked detectable pSmad1/5 signal.
source: While wild-type embryos formed a gradient of pSmad1/5 expression that peaks ventrally and decreases dorsally (Figure 2a; Mucha et al., 2018), Acvr1l-KD embryos lacked detectable pSmad1/5 signal (Figure 2a').
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a'.

claim: The mean nuclear pSmad1/5 fluorescence of Acvr1l-KD embryos was significantly decreased compared to WT embryos.
source: The mean nuclear pSmad1/5 fluorescence of Acvr1l-KD embryos was significantly decreased compared to WT embryos (Figure 2h).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2h.

claim: Injected mouse Acvr1 mRNA did not alter the pSmad1/5 gradient in WT embryos and rescued pSmad1/5 in Acvr1l-KD embryos.
source: Injected mouse Acvr1 mRNA did not alter the pSmad1/5 gradient in WT embryos and rescued pSmad1/5 in Acvr1l-KD embryos (Figure 2b,b').
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b,b'.

claim: There was no significant difference in mean nuclear pSmad1/5 intensity between uninjected wild-type, Acvr1-injected wild-type, and Acvr1l-KD embryos injected and rescued with Acvr1.
source: There was no significant difference in mean nuclear pSmad1/5 intensity between uninjected wild-type, Acvr1-injected wild-type, and Acvr1l-KD embryos injected and rescued with Acvr1 (Figure 2h).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2h.

claim: ΔAcvr1 did not perturb normal gradient formation in WT embryos, but could not rescue loss of pSmad1/5 in Acvr1l-KD embryos.
source: ΔAcvr1 also did not perturb normal gradient formation in WT embryos, but could not rescue loss of pSmad1/5 in Acvr1l-KD embryos (Figure 2c,c').
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c,c'.

claim: There was no significant difference in mean pSmad1/5 fluorescence between Acvr1l-KD embryos and Acvr1l-KD embryos injected with ΔAcvr1.
source: There was no significant difference in mean pSmad1/5 fluorescence between Acvr1l-KD embryos and Acvr1l-KD embryos injected with ΔAcvr1, showing that WT-Acvr1 cannot signal through pSmad1/5 without a ligand-binding domain (Figure 2h).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2h.

claim: WT-Acvr1 cannot signal through pSmad1/5 without a ligand-binding domain.
source: There was no significant difference in mean pSmad1/5 fluorescence between Acvr1l-KD embryos and Acvr1l-KD embryos injected with ΔAcvr1, showing that WT-Acvr1 cannot signal through pSmad1/5 without a ligand-binding domain (Figure 2h).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Both Acvr1-R206H and ΔAcvr1-R206H restored pSmad1/5 signaling in Acvr1l-KD embryos and greatly expanded the signaling gradient dorsally.
source: In contrast, both Acvr1-R206H and ΔAcvr1-R206H restored pSmad1/5 signaling in Acvr1l-KD embryos and greatly expanded the signaling gradient dorsally (Figure 2d,d',e,e').
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2d,d',e,e'.

claim: Acvr1-G328R and ΔAcvr1-G328R rescued and expanded the pSmad1/5 gradient even when endogenous Acvr1l was absent.
source: Likewise, Acvr1-G328R and ΔAcvr1-G328R rescued and expanded the pSmad1/5 gradient even when endogenous Acvr1l was absent (Figure 2f,f',g,g').
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2f,f',g,g'.

claim: Both ACVR1-R206H and ACVR1-G328R significantly increased the mean pSmad1/5 signaling intensity in Acvr1l-KD embryos regardless of the presence of a ligand-binding domain.
source: Both ACVR1-R206H and ACVR1-G328R significantly increased the mean pSmad1/5 signaling intensity in Acvr1l-KD embryos regardless of the presence of a ligand-binding domain (Figure 2h).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2h.

claim: ACVR1-R206H and ACVR1-G328R have acquired the capacity to over-activate Smad1/5 phosphorylation even in the absence of an intact ligand-binding domain.
source: These results confirm that ACVR1-R206H and ACVR1-G328R have acquired the capacity to over-activate Smad1/5 phosphorylation even in the absence of an intact ligand-binding domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Previous studies showed that ACVR1 binds and signals in response to Bmp7.
source: We used Bmp7 in this experiment since previous studies showed that ACVR1 binds and signals in response to Bmp7 (Yadin et al., 2016; Little and Mullins, 2009; Heinecke et al., 2009; Allendorph et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Homozygous bmp7-/- embryos exhibit a severely dorsalized C5 phenotype.
source: Homozygous bmp7-/- embryos exhibit a severely dorsalized C5 phenotype (Figure 3a,b column 1; Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Nguyen et al., 1998; Dick et al., 2000; Schmid et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3 and citations to prior research.

claim: The dorsalization of bmp7-/- embryos can be rescued by injected bmp7 mRNA.
source: This dorsalization can be rescued by injected bmp7 mRNA (Figure 3a,b column 2; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: bmp7 mRNA expression does not rescue bmp7-/- embryos that are also deficient for Acvr1l.
source: However, bmp7 mRNA expression does not rescue bmp7-/- embryos that are also deficient for Acvr1l, as expected (Figure 3a,b column 3; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: In the absence of endogenous bmp7, WT ACVR1 expression cannot rescue bmp7-/- embryos.
source: Conversely, in the absence of endogenous bmp7, WT ACVR1 expression cannot rescue bmp7-/- embryos (Figure 3b column 4, b'; Figure 3—figure supplement 1), confirming that both of these components are required for BMP signaling to pattern the developing embryo.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Both Bmp7 and ACVR1 are required for BMP signaling to pattern the developing embryo.
source: Conversely, in the absence of endogenous bmp7, WT ACVR1 expression cannot rescue bmp7-/- embryos (Figure 3b column 4, b'; Figure 3—figure supplement 1), confirming that both of these components are required for BMP signaling to pattern the developing embryo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Co-injection of human ACVR1 with bmp7 mRNA rescued embryos to less dorsalized or wild-type phenotypes.
source: Co-injection of human ACVR1 with bmp7 mRNA rescued embryos to less dorsalized or wild-type phenotypes (Figure 3b column 5, b'; Fig Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Mouse Acvr1 rescued DV patterning with bmp7 mRNA, but could not pattern embryos in the absence of bmp7.
source: Similarly, mouse Acvr1 rescued DV patterning with bmp7 mRNA, but could not pattern embryos in the absence of bmp7 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, columns 5 and 6).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: ACVR1-R206H rescued bmp7-/-, acvr1l-KD fish primarily to mildly ventralized phenotypes.
source: ACVR1-R206H rescued bmp7-/-, acvr1l-KD fish primarily to mildly ventralized phenotypes (Figure 3c column 4, c'; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The rescue of bmp7-/-, acvr1l-KD embryos by ACVR1-R206H was enhanced to severe ventralization phenotypes by the addition of bmp7 ligand mRNA.
source: This rescue was enhanced to severe ventralization phenotypes by the addition of bmp7 ligand mRNA (Figure 3c column 5, c', Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: ACVR1-G328R rescued bmp7-/- embryos to less severe dorsalized phenotypes.
source: Similarly, ACVR1-G328R rescued bmp7-/- embryos to less severe dorsalized phenotypes (Figure 3d column 4, d', Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and induced further ventralization in response to bmp7 ligand (Figure 3d column 5, d'; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: ACVR1-G328R induced further ventralization in response to bmp7 ligand.
source: Similarly, ACVR1-G328R rescued bmp7-/- embryos to less severe dorsalized phenotypes (Figure 3d column 4, d', Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and induced further ventralization in response to bmp7 ligand (Figure 3d column 5, d'; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Mouse Acvr1 only rescued bmp7-/- mutant fish in the presence of injected bmp7 mRNA.
source: Like human ACVR1, mouse Acvr1 only rescued bmp7-/- mutant fish in the presence of injected bmp7 mRNA (Figure 3e, columns 5 and 6; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3e and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: ΔAcvr1 could not rescue bmp7-/- embryos regardless of the presence of Bmp7.
source: ΔAcvr1, however, could not rescue bmp7-/- embryos regardless of the presence of Bmp7 (Figure 3e, columns 7 and 8; Figure 3—figure supplement 2), demonstrating that WT Acvr1 requires a ligand-binding domain to signal.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3e and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: WT Acvr1 requires a ligand-binding domain to signal.
source: ΔAcvr1, however, could not rescue bmp7-/- embryos regardless of the presence of Bmp7 (Figure 3e, columns 7 and 8; Figure 3—figure supplement 2), demonstrating that WT Acvr1 requires a ligand-binding domain to signal.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Acvr1-R206H rescued bmp7-/-, acvr1l-KD embryos primarily to mildly ventralized phenotypes.
source: Acvr1-R206H rescued bmp7-/-, acvr1l-KD embryos primarily to mildly ventralized phenotypes (Figure 3f, column 5; Figure 3—figure supplement 2) and additional bmp7 ligand mRNA enhanced the rescue to severely ventralized phenotypes (Figure 3f, column 6; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3f and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Additional bmp7 ligand mRNA enhanced the rescue of bmp7-/-, acvr1l-KD embryos by Acvr1-R206H to severely ventralized phenotypes.
source: Acvr1-R206H rescued bmp7-/-, acvr1l-KD embryos primarily to mildly ventralized phenotypes (Figure 3f, column 5; Figure 3—figure supplement 2) and additional bmp7 ligand mRNA enhanced the rescue to severely ventralized phenotypes (Figure 3f, column 6; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3f and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: ΔAcvr1-R206H rescued bmp7-/- embryos to ventralized phenotypes.
source: Importantly, while ΔAcvr1-R206H rescued bmp7-/- embryos to ventralized phenotypes (Figure 3e, column 7; Figure 3—figure supplement 2), the addition of bmp7 mRNA did not further enhance ventralization (Figure 3e, column 8; Figure 3—figure supplement 2), supporting that loss of the ligand-binding domain prevents ligand response.
